key_insight: UniT introduces chain-of-thought style, test-time iterative refinement for a single unified multimodal model, letting the model decompose, verify, and correct outputs at inference without retraining. This test-time scaling (TTS) approach improves compositional and spatial reasoning by adaptively allocating extra inference compute.
problem_solved: Overcomes the one-pass limitation of unified multimodal models on tasks that require decomposition, multi-step verification, or iterative correction (e.g., complex spatial compositions and interacting objects).
method: Embed chain-of-thought (CoT) style intermediate reasoning into the unified multimodal architecture at inference, producing and checking substeps (decompose → predict → verify → correct).
Apply Test-Time Scaling (TTS): adaptively allocate extra inference passes/compute (progressive unrolling, reranking or iterative editing) to hard examples without model finetuning.
Demonstrate gains on multimodal tasks requiring spatial and compositional reasoning, showing a controllable accuracy vs. latency trade-off.
impact: Provides a practical, deployable knob (more inference compute) to substantially boost performance on complex multimodal tasks without retraining, enabling better compositional reasoning and flexible latency–quality tradeoffs for practitioners.
visual_elements: Iterative inference loop diagram (input → decompose CoT steps → verify → correct → final output)
Before/after multimodal example (single-pass output vs. UniT iterative-refined output) highlighting corrected spatial/compositional errors
Compute vs. accuracy curve showing test-time scaling trade-off (more passes → higher accuracy)
Unified model schematic showing single architecture handling vision + language with embedded CoT tokens
paper_title: UniT: Unified Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Test-time Scaling
paper_authors: Leon Liangyu Chen, Haoyu Ma, Zhipeng Fan, Ziqi Huang, Animesh Sinha
